title: A torsion-free group algebra with zero divisors
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: An exposition of OpenAI's disproof (2026) of Kaplansky's zero-divisor conjecture: there are a finitely presented torsion-free group G, with a finite two-dimensional classifying space, and nonzero elements alpha, beta of F_2[G] with alpha beta = 0. The first lesson introduces group algebras and unique products and proves the cancellation mechanism: two immersed labelled graphs whose outgoing letter sets have odd intersections give zero divisors in any group where closed paths have trivial labels. The second builds the alphabet from the projective plane over the field with 128 elements and three extra letters, with prescribed types of odd intersections, turn weights and a decay estimate for squared word weights. The third chooses the graphs by random matchings conditioned on large girth and bounds the probability of prescribed edges and the diameters. The fourth, fifth and sixth prove that with high probability no bounded system of almost completely paired paths exists: image graphs and multiplicity stages, aligned blocks, link components and word counts, and a product bound that selects one stage. The seventh and eighth define reduced spherical arrangements, close long paths cheaply, bound comparison intervals by Euler characteristics, and extract a bounded system from every arrangement by recursive planar separation. The ninth attaches cones along the components of the graph and shows by minimal cone pictures and band surgery that the complex is aspherical and the roots are separated. The tenth proves torsion-freeness through the cellular resolution, the comparison theorem and the periodic resolution of a cyclic group, and completes the proof.
prerequisites: core course Abstract Algebra II (Judson, Abstract Algebra: Theory and Applications): the field with 128 elements (Theorem 22.1.6), coordinates and dimension in vector spaces (Propositions 20.3.1 and 20.3.6)
core course Algebraic Topology (Fomberg's notes): homotopy invariance of singular homology (Theorem 1.13, Corollary 1.14)
programme lesson Explicit CW models and the first Hurewicz map (course CG-S6), Theorem 4.1: the Hurewicz theorem
programme lesson Schubert cells and universal Grassmannian cohomology (course DG-CHAR), Lemma 2.1: cellular homology of finite CW complexes
programme lesson Homotopy fibres and the Serre spectral sequence (course DG-CHAR), Section B.4: Whitehead's theorem for CW complexes
finite probability: expectations, Markov's inequality and the union bound

checks.reading: The manuscript 'A Torsion-Free Group Algebra with Zero Divisors' (OpenAI, 23 Sep 2026; paper.tex with the introduction and main theorem, sections types 170 lines, entropy 548, planar 423, topology 113, factors 34, two figures, references.bib; local clone openai-math-20261006) was read in full on 15 Oct 2026, and every step was derived again while the lessons were written: the projective plane counts, the types and their odd intersections, the turn weights and the squared-word estimate with its exact fractions; the matching model, girth conditioning by switchings, the prescription bound and the diameter bound by expansion; systems and pairings, the cycle rank of image graphs by non-backtracking walks, chains and the multiplicity bound, patterns and the stage balance; the common grid by simultaneous approximation, alignment, joins, propagation, self-links, link balance, bins and enlarged patterns; fixed and permitted letters, the product bound and the selection of one stage; short closures; the planar interval lemma with Euler characteristics and the good-gap involution; recursive separation, the parameter order and the extraction of a cluster; cone pictures through the model with disks, tightening, pairing arcs, the four cases of band surgery and essentiality in the universal cover; asphericity, the cellular resolution, the comparison theorem and the periodic resolution; the zero divisors. No error found. Additions and changes of form in the course: essential spheres are defined through the second homology of the universal cover, and a lemma derives pi_2(X) = 0 from their absence by the Hurewicz theorem; in the comparison of the cone with the model with disks, only the vanishing of pi_1 and pi_2 of the model is used, with H_2 computed from spanning-tree loops by the cellular boundary formula, not its contractibility; the higher homotopy groups of the cover are shown to vanish by induction with the Hurewicz theorem, and contractibility of the cover follows by Whitehead's theorem; the comparison theorem for resolutions is proved; the closure cost is bounded by 2D/U instead of 3D/U; the drawing of the piece graph is given in polar coordinates; the four cases of band surgery are written out with the endpoints of all paths and both contractions. The Lean formalization in the release (scope note lean/docs/196.md, comparator statement ComparatorChallenges/TorsionFreeZeroDivisors.lean, whose classifying space is a finite connected 2-dimensional CW complex with a contractible covering space; 124 files in OAI/Algebra/GroupRing, none containing sorry, among them files whose text mentions separators, the Hurewicz or Whitehead theorems or Euler characteristics, identified by text search) was not built or run, and it was not checked which of the named statements of the course it proves in the form used here. Later literature, read on 15 Oct 2026 in an arXiv search for preprints after the release: Ivanov arXiv:2610.17662 (13 Oct 2026; Theorem 1.1, Corollary 1.2, Sections 1, 2 and 8, Appendices A and B), which extends the theorem to every odd characteristic with a signed cancellation, a design over the projective plane over F_(p^3) and a bipartite random model, keeps the geometric part, and records a line-by-line check of OpenAI's argument: no error affecting the conclusions, six points that deserve a clarifying sentence (the count r_n and the injectivity in the switching lemma, kappa < 1/2 for joins, the frequencies on side A, same-arc digons, the bound m <= 2h/(UL), and the exterior cases of band surgery), each of which the lessons treat explicitly; Mian-Siddique arXiv:2609.22380 (abstract; a Lean-checked proof that Gardam's A_2-tilde lattice fails unique products). Integrated: the odd-characteristic theorem and its signed cancellation lemma (first lesson, Section 4 and Exercise 5.6), the odd-characteristic design (second lesson), the observation that same-arc digons do not occur over the graphs (seventh lesson), and the status in characteristic zero (last lesson). Free sources read on 15 Oct 2026: Lipton-Tarjan, Stanford report STAN-CS-77-627 (abstract, Theorem 4 and Corollary 2); Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, free edition (the statements cited); Gardam arXiv:2102.11818 (introduction and bibliography); first pages of Ollivier arXiv:math/0310022, Gruber arXiv:1210.0178 and Bereznyuk arXiv:1711.05293; the programme lessons cited as prerequisites (statements and proofs of the cited results). open_obligations: Named statements used without proof in the course, each with its exact statement and free locators in the lesson where it is stated: (SURF) facts on regular neighbourhoods and surfaces in the sphere: Euler characteristics of the regions, planar regions with b boundary circles have Euler characteristic 2 - b, opposite boundary orientations, and the Schoenflies consequence that the closure of the complement of a closed disk is a disk and that of a closed annulus two disks (seventh lesson, Section 3; locators in Hatcher, Algebraic Topology: Theorem 2.44, Section 2.2, Corollary 3.45, Proposition 2B.1); (SEP) the planar separator theorem of Lipton and Tarjan (eighth lesson, Section 1; Corollary 2 of their Stanford report STAN-CS-77-627); (PI1) fundamental groups of graphs and of 2-cell attachments (Hatcher, Propositions 1A.2 and 1.26); (COV) universal covers of CW complexes, lifting of maps and homotopies, deck transformations and higher homotopy groups of covers (Hatcher, Section 1.3, Propositions 1.30, 1.33, 1.34, 1.39, 4.1); (CELL) cellular homology of CW complexes of dimension two with the cellular boundary formula and the augmented complex, and the fundamental class of a triangulated sphere (Hatcher, Lemma 2.34, Theorem 2.35, Theorem 2.27, Section 3.3; the finite case is proved in the programme, Schubert cells and universal Grassmannian cohomology, Lemma 2.1); (PL) triangulation and simplicial approximation, and transverse preimages of edge midpoints for maps from surfaces to graphs (Hatcher, Theorem 2C.1 and its proof); all in the ninth lesson, Section 2. A foundation course proving them is requested from the programme coordinator.
The lessons were written and checked by one model in one session; they have not been checked by a second reader.
